item.title: Permissions by Role
item.description:
This page tells you which Kanvas actions require a permission, which default roles grant each permission, and which actions are limited by something other than a permission. Use it to find out why an action is missing for a user and which role grants it.

How permissions work 🔗

A permission is a named key, such as Deploy Design, that allows one action. Keys are grouped into keychains, and a role bundles one or more keychains. Your organization assigns roles to users. Before Kanvas offers certain actions, it checks whether the user holds the matching key. Kanvas uses the shared Layer5 permission set and defines no permissions of its own. See Roles and Keychains.

item.title: Roles and Permissions
item.description:
This page tells you which permissions each default Layer5 Cloud role holds. Use it to find out why an action is missing for a user and which role grants it. For how roles, keychains, and permissions fit together, see Roles.

How permission checks work 🔗

A permission is a named key that allows one action, such as Create Team. A keychain groups keys, and a role groups keychains. Layer5 Cloud checks the key, never the role name. Before it runs a guarded action, Cloud resolves the organization the request names, then checks whether the user holds the key through a role in that organization. A user’s permissions are the union of the keys from every role the user holds there.

item.title: Security Reference
item.description:
This page states how keys, keychains, tokens, and sessions behave, exactly, as of Layer5 Cloud v1.0.280. For the model, read the Keys, Keychains, Sessions, and Tokens concepts. For tasks, use the security guides. For base URL, authentication, and the organization header, see the Cloud API. All paths below sit under /api unless noted.

Permission keys 🔗

Provider Admin holds every key. The table lists the default holders of the other roles. “Interface” means the control or tab is disabled or replaced by a permission error screen. “Server” means the Layer5 Cloud server refuses the request with HTTP 403.

item.title: Build a Custom Keychain
item.description:
A custom keychain bundles the keys that a custom role needs. This guide creates a keychain, changes its keys, and deletes it. It is written for Provider Admins and self-hosted operators, because only a Provider Admin can create, change, or delete a keychain, or include it in a role. For the model, read the Keychains concept.

Before you start 🔗

  • You need the Provider Admin role. The interface also checks the Create Keychain, Edit Keychain, and Delete Keychain permissions for the matching controls. Provider Admin holds all three. No other default role does.
  • A keychain does nothing until a role includes it. Creating and editing roles is a Provider Admin action. On hosted Layer5 Cloud an organization cannot complete this path alone. On a self-hosted deployment, your Provider Admins can.
  • Keychains are not organization-scoped. A role that includes your keychain grants its keys to every user who holds that role, in every organization.

Create a keychain 🔗

Open the Keychains tab under Security and create a keychain. Give it a name and choose the keys it bundles. Layer5 Cloud creates the keychain and adds each key to it. If adding a key fails, the interface reports it as “Failed to add key to keychain”. Open the keychain and confirm every key you chose is present.

item.title: Keychains
item.description:
A keychain is a named bundle of keys. It sits between the single permission and the role a person holds:

  • A key allows one action, such as Create Token.
  • A keychain groups related keys, such as everything needed to manage teams.
  • A role groups keychains, and users hold roles in an organization or team.

A user’s effective keys in an organization are the union of the keys in every keychain of every role the user holds there. A keychain grants nothing by itself. It takes effect only through a role that includes it.
